text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Trade unions, employers and the government held talks on the unions demand that the minimum salary should be raised to 1,200 kroons per month.
SONUMILEHT

- The government has refused to allocate an extra 4.5 million kroons for the repair of the tax department building, although it says it needs 30 million kroons for the repair before it can move to the new building.

- State Prosecutor Indrek Meelak criticises the draft law on his office for subordinating prosecution to politics. The justice ministry argues that the prosecution is defending its departmental interests.
- The ruling coalition is launching a discussion of economic policy aimed at the development of domestic industry. The initiator was the Coalition Party, the leading coalition party.
EESTI PAEVALEHT

- The Estonia ferry disaster investigation commission met divers who entered the wreck. The meeting helped overcome some confusion caused by the videotapes of the dives and ended suspicions that some of the footage was edited afterwards.

- Arnold Ruutel, parliament vice-chairman, will not require the aditional rooms, car and bodyguards to which he is eligible according to the law on presidential privileges. Ruutel headed the parliament praesidium until 1992 and the post is considered equal to that of the president.

- Tartu University medical faculty held a vote of no confidence in the rector after the amendment to the law on the university which joins the budgets of the clinical department and the university. The medics fear that this will enable the university to restrict their rights and funding.
POSTIMEES

- Two Estonian authors, the novelist Jaan Kross and the poet and essayist Jaan Kaplinski, have been put up as candidates of the Nobel literature prize; some Swedish sources have speculated about Kaplinski having better chances.

- Estonian state officials are still confused about the comment by U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry about the exclusion of the Baltic states from NATO enlargement. Defence Minister Andrus Oovel has been accused by the press of having failed to inform the government and parliament.
- The Estonian theatre festival was opened in Tartu yesterday, restoring a previous tradition of annual festivals. Sixteen state-financed and private theatres are represented.
ARIPAEV
- The forming of a Estonian-U.S. joint venture for energy production may fail, since the parties have not yet agreed on any details.
- The U.S. project of a technology park near Tallin is at a standstill due to problems with property rights and opposition of bureaucrats.
- Transit through Estonian ports decreased two percent in the first half of 1996 versus 1995 and the fall was mainly in the export of metal and grain.
